Check LPPLS Estimates Against the Admissibility Conditions

Source: R/lppls_admissible.R
lppls_admissible.Rd

A calibration is admissible when its estimate meets the conditions fit_lppls() works with: m and omega inside their bounds, B below upper[3], and the damping D at least lower[4] (Filimonov, Demos & Sornette, 2017). fit_lppls() bounds its search in m and omega, but checks B and D only on the result of each search, and print.lppls_fit() reports how many results were out of range. lppls_admissible() applies the same conditions to any set of estimates: the estimate of a fit, its per-tc fits, every window of a rolling calibration, or a data frame of estimates.

Usage

lppls_admissible(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lppls_fit'
lppls_admissible(
  x,
  which = c("estimate", "fits"),
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lppls_rolling'
lppls_admissible(x, lower = NULL, upper = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
lppls_admissible(x, lower = NULL, upper = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

An "lppls_fit" from fit_lppls(), an "lppls_rolling" from lppls_rolling(), or estimates with elements m, omega, B and D: a data frame with one row per estimate, or a list holding one estimate, such as fit$fit[[1]].

...

Not used.

which

For an "lppls_fit": "estimate" (the default) checks the reported estimate, "fits" every per-tc fit (every restart in mode "F1"), including those the B filter set aside.

lower, upper

Numeric vectors of length 4, bounds for c(m, omega, B, D) as in fit_lppls(). By default the bounds the calibration was run with; for a data frame or a list, the defaults of fit_lppls().

Value

The estimates checked, as a data frame with one row per estimate and five logical columns added: m_ok, omega_ok, B_ok, D_ok, and admissible, which is TRUE when all four are. A missing value counts as out of range.

Details

The conditions are those of fit_lppls(): lower[1] <= m <= upper[1], lower[2] <= omega <= upper[2], B < upper[3] and D >= lower[4]. lower[3] and upper[4] are not used.

The share of admissible windows in a rolling calibration, mean(lppls_admissible(roll)$admissible), measures how consistently a bubble signal holds up as the window start moves.

References

Filimonov, V., Demos, G., & Sornette, D. (2017). Modified profile likelihood inference and interval forecast of the burst of financial bubbles. Quantitative Finance, 17(8), 1167-1186. doi:10.1080/14697688.2016.1276298

See also

fit_lppls(), print.lppls_fit(), lppls_rolling()

Examples

set.seed(4)
log_p <- eval_lppls(1:200, A = 8, B = -0.025, C1 = 0.0015, C2 = 0.001,
                    tc = 221, m = 0.6, omega = 8) + rnorm(200, sd = 0.01)
fit <- fit_lppls(log_p, fh = 30, mode = "MPL",
                 m_init = 0.5, o_init = 8, num_searches = 2)

## The reported estimate
lppls_admissible(fit)
#>         tc         m    omega        A          B            C1         C2
#> 1 222.9766 0.5937427 8.258585 8.010661 -0.0261428 -0.0006679849 0.00169013
#>          D     value m_ok omega_ok B_ok D_ok admissible
#> 1 1.034206 0.0178573 TRUE     TRUE TRUE TRUE       TRUE

## Every per-tc fit, against a stricter damping floor of 1
adm <- lppls_admissible(fit, which = "fits", lower = c(0.1, 6, -1e14, 1))
mean(adm$admissible)
#> [1] 1
